analysis.summary: ABS Marine Services Limited published its Investor Presentation for H1 FY27, highlighting revenue from operations of ₹164.75 Crores and profit after tax of ₹43.07 Crores. The company expanded its owned fleet to 12 vessels following the delivery and Indian-flag registration of ARTEMIS and SERENITY. Operating cash flow reached ₹150.59 Crores, and long-term deployment charters were secured with major energy players including Hardy E&P and Oil India. ABS Marine Services Limited reported strong financial performance for FY26, driven by owned fleet expansion, disciplined execution, and cost management. Total income reached INR322.64 crores, EBITDA increased to INR152.55 crores, and profit after tax rose to INR80.80 crores.

guidance.claim: Management stated that its revenue growth guidance of about 10% over FY26 was conservative.
guidance.quote: We always try to be very conservative and like to perform better than what we have given.

guidance.claim: Management expects a 10 percent increase in turnover for the current financial year assuming all vessels run in the second half.
guidance.quote: As regards the guidance on the top line is concerned, we can expect a 10% increase -- assuming that all the vessels will be running in the second half.

guidance.claim: Management stated that the EBITDA margin band of 45 to 50 percent will continue.
guidance.quote: As regards the EBITDA is concerned, I am sure that currently it is in the band of 45 to 50. I am sure that that will continue.

guidance.claim: Management expects the tax rate for FY27 to be around a maximum of 1.5% to 2%.
guidance.quote: Around maximum of 1.5% to 2% in that range.

demand_outlook.claim: Management outlined key priorities for FY27 regarding fleet utilization and tender bidding.
demand_outlook.quote: Keep owned-fleet utilisation high, convert short-term deployments into long-term charters and keep bidding for tenders from oil majors and port authorities.

demand_outlook.claim: Management stated that favorable demand-supply dynamics in the offshore vessel market continue to improve utilization levels and charter rates across segments.
demand_outlook.quote: Additionally, favorable demand-supply dynamics in the offshore vessel market, supported by an aging global fleet and limited new vessel additions, continue to improve utilization levels and charter rates across segments.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted that ONGC is talking about a 20-vessel tender coming up anytime soon.
demand_outlook.quote: ONGC is asking for about 20-vessel tender is going to come.

capex_expansion.claim: During H2 FY26, the company successfully inducted the offshore support vessel Artemis into its owned fleet.
capex_expansion.quote: As part of this strategy, during H2 FY26, we successfully inducted the offshore support vessel, Artemis, into our owned fleet, expanding our vessel ownership portfolio and improving our ability to participate in higher-value offshore projects.

capex_expansion.claim: The company is scheduled to take delivery of an offshore supply vessel in Q1 FY27.
capex_expansion.quote: Further enhancing our offshore capabilities, we are also scheduled to take delivery of an offshore supply vessel in Q1 FY27.

capex_expansion.claim: Management stated they have spent a total of about $15 million for both the new vessels, Hades and MPSV.
capex_expansion.quote: Just a moment. We have totally, we have spent about $15 million for both the vessels.

margins_costs.claim: Owned vessel economics shift ownership costs to depreciation and interest below EBITDA.
margins_costs.quote: Owned vessels earn the full day rate; ownership costs move to depreciation and interest, below EBITDA.

margins_costs.claim: On a consolidated basis, total income for FY26 stood at INR322.64 crores, registering a growth of 75.05% year-on-year.
margins_costs.quote: On a consolidated basis, total income stood at INR322.64 crores, registering a robust growth of 75.05% year-on-year.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA increased significantly by 179.17% to INR152.55 crores, with the EBITDA margin expanding by 1,763 basis points to 47.28% in FY26.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA increased significantly by 179.17% to INR152.55 crores, while the EBITDA margin expanded sharply by 1,763 basis points to 47.28%.

margins_costs.claim: Profit after tax for FY26 rose by 196.45% to INR80.80 crores, with the PAT margin improving by 1,026 basis points to 25.04%.
margins_costs.quote: Profit after tax rose by 196.45% to INR80.80 crores, with a PAT margin improving by 1,026 basis points to 25.04%.

margins_costs.claim: Management stated that the ballpoint figure for the daily cost of an idle vessel is about $1,700.
margins_costs.quote: So, let's put it as a ballpoint figure, it's about $1,700 a day.

margins_costs.claim: Improved utilization levels, better margin realization, and disciplined cost management contributed to growth in revenue and profitability.
margins_costs.quote: Improved utilization levels, better margin realization, and disciplined cost management have contributed to healthy growth in both revenue and profitability.

orders_capacity.claim: ABS Marine secured a five-year charter for ARTEMIS with Hardy E&P, ONGC, and Invenire.
orders_capacity.quote: We fixed ARTEMIS on a firm five-year charter with Hardy Exploration & Production (India) Inc., acting for itself and its joint venture partners ONGC and Invenire Petrodyne, which gives us strong revenue visibility.

orders_capacity.claim: Management stated that out of eight owned vessels, five are on long-term charter, two have just come out of charter, and a third newly acquired one is going to dry dock.
orders_capacity.quote: Out of the eight vessels that we own, five of them are on long-term charter, three of them -- two of them have just come out of charter, and third one is just we have acquired, so it has to go into the dry dock and then only come out and then only we put her in the market.

orders_capacity.claim: Management stated that the company operates a total of 12 vessels, including four smaller vessels on long-term charter.
orders_capacity.quote: No, 12 number is correct. The other four vessels are smaller vessels, they are on long-term charter.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management noted that Emerald was pulled out for upcoming dry docking and is currently at anchorage.
risks_headwinds.quote: Whereas Emerald, we had to pull out because the dry docking was coming up, so some jobs were to be done. So, we have pulled out and as of now, she is at the anchorage and we are negotiating with various people for the next contract.

management_commitments.claim: Management aims to keep owned-fleet utilization high and convert short-term deployments into long-term charters during FY27.
management_commitments.quote: Keep owned-fleet utilisation high, convert short-term deployments into long-term charters and keep bidding for tenders from oil majors and port authorities.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that the company is scheduled to take delivery of an offshore supply vessel in Q1 FY27.
management_commitments.quote: Further enhancing our offshore capabilities, we are also scheduled to take delivery of an offshore supply vessel in Q1 FY27.

management_commitments.claim: Management expects a 10 percent increase in turnover for the current financial year assuming all vessels run in the second half.
management_commitments.quote: As regards the guidance on the top line is concerned, we can expect a 10% increase -- assuming that all the vessels will be running in the second half.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that the tax rate for FY27 is expected to be around a maximum of 1.5% to 2%.
management_commitments.quote: Around maximum of 1.5% to 2% in that range.
